userRequest: lass uns den neuen testplan umsetzen

scope.summary: Execute the deterministic Pros end-user setup test plan from a fresh end-user perspective.
inScope: Inventory local prerequisites and current client/MCP state
Back up and wipe only approved Pros-managed MCP client entries
Install or update global pros CLI and verify auth safely
Initialize a fresh case folder outside the source repository
Install/update global tool skills without overwriting foreign skills
Prepare HubSpot MCP auth app and credentials through safe stdin/credential-store paths
Run the canonical README Mistral/OpenCode workflow starting with /werkzeuge-mcp-einrichtung
Verify AnythingLLM HubSpot MCP through @agent stream-chat plus WebSocket
Run isolated Serena smoke test in a throwaway project
Run secret-safety checks and reconcile README/runtime documentation with observed behavior
outOfScope: Deleting HubSpot OS credential-store entries without separate explicit approval
Testing Serena against real user projects or memories
Posting secrets, OAuth codes, client secrets, tokens, or credential values in chat or files

requirements.description: Test must simulate a clean end-user setup while preserving unrelated local configuration.
requirements.acceptance: Inventory, backups, dry-runs, and explicit approval gates exist before any destructive or write operation.

requirements.description: HubSpot credentials and OAuth materials must remain secret-safe.
requirements.acceptance: Secrets are supplied only through stdin or OS credential store; no secret values are logged, committed, or pasted.

requirements.description: Mistral/OpenCode must execute the runtime MCP workflow from the fresh case folder.
requirements.acceptance: Prompt begins with /werkzeuge-mcp-einrichtung and evidence shows runtime workflow plus pros-runtime-manifest were used.

requirements.description: OpenCode and AnythingLLM HubSpot MCP setup must be verified through their real client paths.
requirements.acceptance: OpenCode shows HubSpot connected after OAuth; AnythingLLM agent invocation exposes hubspot-* tools through WebSocket evidence.

requirements.description: Serena must be tested in isolation only.
requirements.acceptance: Throwaway project has its own .serena/project.yml and logs show that project, not real user project paths.

requirements.description: Every deviation must become a bug, doc-fix, accepted decision, or release follow-up.
requirements.acceptance: Final deviation ledger links each issue to an artifact or explicit decision.

contracts.apiContractRationale: This is an operational end-to-end test execution plan. It exercises existing CLIs, client configs, OAuth, MCP runtimes, and documentation; it does not introduce a new cross-boundary API.

operationalContracts.name: approval-gate-contract
operationalContracts.rule: Any command that writes client config, wipes entries, stores credentials, or performs OAuth-sensitive setup requires explicit user approval after inventory or dry-run evidence.

operationalContracts.name: secret-handling-contract
operationalContracts.rule: Secrets are never requested in chat; stdin-only or OS credential-store paths are used, and outputs are redacted.

operationalContracts.name: mcp-config-scope-contract
operationalContracts.rule: Only planned Pros-managed or explicitly user-approved test entries may be removed or changed; unrelated entries are preserved.

operationalContracts.name: fallordner-contract
operationalContracts.rule: Fresh case folder must be outside the source repository and all test evidence must avoid secrets.

operationalContracts.name: anythingllm-proof-contract
operationalContracts.rule: AnythingLLM verification requires @agent stream-chat plus WebSocket /api/agent-invocation/<uuid>; any CLI alone is insufficient.

operationalContracts.name: serena-isolation-contract
operationalContracts.rule: Serena smoke test must use a throwaway project with its own .serena/project.yml and must not alter real memories or project configs.

assumptions: The user wants to execute the plan, not redesign it from scratch.
The current host is the intended Windows test host.
User will provide explicit approvals and secret input only through safe terminal/stdin flows when needed.
AnythingLLM Desktop/backend and OpenCode CLI may require local state checks before later steps can proceed.

alternativesConsidered.option: Execute the entire test plan automatically in one pass
alternativesConsidered.rationale: The plan contains write, wipe, credential, OAuth, and desktop-client steps that require approval gates and secret-safe handoffs.

alternativesConsidered.option: Run only read-only inventory first, then proceed gate by gate
alternativesConsidered.rationale: Minimizes risk, preserves unrelated local state, and matches the existing plan constraints.

alternativesConsidered.option: Use the older first-use setup plan as the execution basis
alternativesConsidered.rationale: The deterministic setup plan supersedes the earlier plan and includes later AnythingLLM, Mistral, and Serena isolation findings.

tasks.title: Read-only host inventory and prerequisites
acceptance: OpenCode CLI, AnythingLLM, Node/npm, pros, and pros-mcp-hubspot-remote availability documented
Relevant config paths and current MCP keys inventoried without mutation
Blockers reported before proceeding

tasks.title: Back up and safely wipe approved Pros-managed MCP config
acceptance: Backups exist outside repo with hashes
Dry-runs completed before writes
User explicitly approves any wipe
Only approved entries removed

tasks.title: Install/update pros CLI and verify auth
acceptance: Global @pro-select/pros-cli release/version documented
pros auth status succeeds or stdin-only auth path is used
No registry or release token appears in output

tasks.title: Initialize fresh end-user case folder
acceptance: Case folder is outside source repo
pros init succeeds
pros doctor is green or warnings are explained

tasks.title: Install/update global tool skills
acceptance: pros tools and pros tools update dry-run executed
Actual update occurs only when safe
Foreign/non-Pros-managed skills are not overwritten

tasks.title: Prepare HubSpot MCP credentials
acceptance: Redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:19876/oauth/callback is confirmed
pros mcp hubspot credentials status is ready or user is prompted for stdin-only setup
No client secret is written to chat, repo, fallordner, or client config

tasks.title: Run canonical README Mistral/OpenCode workflow
acceptance: OpenCode/Mistral starts from the case folder
Prompt begins with /werkzeuge-mcp-einrichtung
Mistral reads runtime workflow and pros-runtime-manifest
Mistral uses pros mcp configure for OpenCode and AnythingLLM

tasks.title: Verify OpenCode HubSpot MCP
acceptance: pros mcp status opencode is ready
opencode mcp list shows hubspot connected after OAuth or a clear OAuth next step

tasks.title: Verify AnythingLLM HubSpot MCP through Agent/WebSocket
acceptance: pros mcp status anythingllm is ready
AnythingLLM workspace slug and backend reachability documented
@agent stream-chat yields websocketUUID
WebSocket evidence shows hubspot-* tools

tasks.title: Run isolated Serena smoke test
acceptance: Throwaway project outside real projects created
.serena/project.yml exists in throwaway project
Logs show throwaway project activation
Real Serena memories/configs remain unchanged

tasks.title: Run safety, documentation, and deviation closure checks
acceptance: pros doctor is green or all warnings are explained
No secrets found in repo, fallordner, logs, or client configs
README/runtime docs match observed flow or have documented fixes
Every deviation is linked to bug/doc-fix/accepted decision/release step

notes: All 14 source-plan tasks are mapped into 11 execution tasks with dependencies.
Secret handling, MCP wipe scope, Mistral workflow, AnythingLLM WebSocket proof, and Serena isolation are explicitly represented.
Acceptance criteria preserve the original Done When conditions.
Review checked source plan, memory summary, prior execution memory, constraints, and Done When list.
Remaining uncertainty is explicitly listed as assumptions rather than hidden in implementation.
No new APIs, abstractions, or automation framework are proposed.
Execution is gate-by-gate because write/credential/OAuth actions require user approvals.
Tasks consolidate documentation and deviation closure into one final P1 task to avoid process bloat.

implementationDomainCheck.summary: Phase 2 IMPL is a no-op for Backend, Frontend, and Mobile because the approved scope is operational QA test execution, not product feature implementation.

attempts.reason: Short agent IDs were not found by OpenCode/OMA and fell back to the default agent. No progress/result memory was written.
All three domain agents completed read-only checks and confirmed no code implementation is required for their domains.

backend.evidence: Plan scope is qa-test-execution; apiContractNeeded is false; tasks are assigned to qa or qa/docs/pm.

frontend.evidence: No UI, React, CSS, component, or frontend feature work is listed; tasks are operational setup/verification tasks.

mobile.evidence: No mobile terms or mobile deliverables are present; tasks are operational setup/verification tasks.
